nc_nose_area.blurb: One of the earliest sections developed on Looking Glass Rock, the big dome in the middle of Pisgah National Forest. Twelve climbs here, nearly all of them trad with a single bolted line, running from the high 5.8 range up to one 5.12. Most of the grades sit between 5.10 and 5.11, and the better-known lines are long four-pitch outings, with plenty of moderates for parties that want something approachable. The base is a short uphill hike on a worn trail, and the area's signature line draws the most traffic, so expect company on the easier routes.

nc_hidden_wall.blurb: A small, steep, tucked-away wall on the north side of Looking Glass Rock. All twelve routes are trad, from 5.8 up to 5.12, and most of them are 5.10 or harder, so this is more a place for experienced leaders than for a first multi-pitch day. Expect thin, bold face climbing with in-cut edges and a crack or two, plus a couple of two-pitch lines. It makes a good spot for less crowded climbing when the main north side routes are busy, and the north side sections stay shady enough to be workable in summer.

nc_east_cliff.blurb: The east of the two cliffs at Melrose Mountain Climbing Park near Tryon. A dozen routes, split evenly between sport and trad, with grades from 5.6 to 5.11 and the bulk of them around 5.9 and 5.10. The gneiss is steep to overhanging, up to about 90 feet high, with a solid cap forming roofs over softer, more brittle rock below, so a helmet is wise. The face looks south and picks up sun for much of the day, and the top of the cliff gives views toward South Carolina. Getting down is steep and effortful, which keeps it adventurous.
nc_east_cliff.parking_note: Park in the existing shoulder pull-offs along the south side of Hogback Mountain Road. Space is limited to a few vehicles, so go early or carpool.
nc_east_cliff.approach: There is no maintained trail. Follow steep climber paths south and downhill from the road to the base; the slope is loose and the walk back out is slower than the way in.

nc_13_two_pitch_wall.blurb: A west-facing wall near the north end of the summit ridge at Crowders Mountain, one of the taller faces in the park. All twelve routes are trad, ranging from an easy 5.4 up to about 5.10, with the largest share in the 5.8 range. The short two-pitch lines, with blocky ledges and big holds, make it a common spot for a first trad lead on standard gear. Climbs start from a ledge above the trail, and you walk off the top to the south.

nc_trundlasaurus_wall.blurb: The largest wall in the Resurgence area of Crowders Mountain, below the Red Wall. It holds twelve routes, a mix of trad and sport with some top-rope options, from 5.6 up to a single 5.11, and most of them in the 5.8 to 5.10 range. It sees little traffic compared with the main crags. The face gets morning sun and falls into shade later in the day, so choose your season accordingly; a small cave near one sport line stays cooler in the morning.
nc_trundlasaurus_wall.approach: Descend past the right end of the Red Wall, go by the New Policy Wall, and continue beyond the Plane Above Your Head Wall on a faint trail to the base.
